results.evidence: The reader's internal resolution (65 ft) is not supported: both waypoints sit on the same crag coordinate, and the 4585 'trailhead' elevation is the Citidel area's listed elevation, not the road end. USGS 3DEP gives ~4,670 ft at the crag coordinate and ~4,230-4,250 ft at the end of the left-fork road spur (located from OSM geometry of FS 9070-310), implying roughly 450 ft of gain, but the crag coordinate is itself approximate and no source states the approach gain. Neither 750 nor 65 can be adopted from two agreeing sources; waypoint[0].elev (4585) also looks wrong for a road-end trailhead but its pin sits on the crag, so it is not patched.

The route's own page lists protection as 12 bolts with chains at top. Inside the row, pro_needs (12 quickdraws), detailed_rack (12 bolts), beta and pitch_detail (12 bolts) all agree; alpine_draws=10 is the lone outlier. No second independent source exists for this obscure 2020 route (other listings mirror the same page).

results.correct_value: The crag and route are documented (Sofa King Buttress, The Citidel, Silver Basin near Snoqualmie Pass; FA Wylie Moreshead 2020; 12 bolts to chains). rope_note's claim that the area is unindexed and a Washington Pass granite crag is false.

The rock is volcanic metamorphic, not Washington Pass granite. Inside the row, approach, waypoints, beta, fa, pitch_detail, detailed_rack and face all describe this documented Silver Basin crag; rope_note is the outlier. rope_note is rewritten to a neutral gear note; the non-rendered 'corrections' and 'gear_confidence' fields still carry the stale 'unverified' claim and were left alone.
